keyVerseText: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
rootMeaning: The word συμπάρειμι (sympáreimi) is formed from the Greek preposition σύν (sýn), meaning 'with' or 'together,' combined with πάρειμι, meaning 'to be present' or 'to be at hand.' This etymology highlights a sense of being present alongside or in close association with someone or something, emphasizing not just mere presence but a shared or accompanied presence. This adds depth beyond the simple English gloss 'are here present,' suggesting an intimate or active presence together rather than mere physical proximity.
usageInScripture: This verb appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Acts 25:24, where it is translated as 'are here present.' The single occurrence underscores its meaning of being physically and relationally present with others. The consistent sense of the word involves being at hand or alongside, whether referring to people or even metaphorically to desires or advocates, as the lexicon notes. The limited usage suggests a precise and deliberate choice to convey togetherness or accompaniment in the narrative context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding συμπάρειμι enriches our grasp of God's relational nature and the fellowship expected among believers. The word's emphasis on being present together reflects the biblical call to communal presence and support, mirroring Christ's promise to be with His followers. It also points to the role of advocates and helpers who stand alongside believers, echoing Christ as our intercessor. Recognizing this helps believers appreciate the importance of mutual presence and divine accompaniment in the Christian life, encouraging faithfulness in both worship and witness.
keyVerseReflection: In Acts 25:24, Festus addresses King Agrippa and those 'who are here present with us,' using συμπάρειμι to emphasize their collective presence and shared witness regarding Paul. This word underscores the gathered assembly's role as active participants in the legal and spiritual drama unfolding. It highlights not just physical proximity but a communal engagement, reminding readers that faith and judgment involve the presence and testimony of the community before God and man.
